DEL-02.evidence: One Python package run from source (answerdesk/, __main__.py); no build, container or deploy automation in examples/born-evolvable.

DEL-03.evidence: Module split by convention (door.py, store.py, desk.py, policy.py). The 'one door' is not enforced: Store methods that write definitions are public (store.py:82-132) and App.seed writes outside the door (app.py:31-51). No import-linter or architecture test in tests/.

DEL-04.evidence: There is no AI implementation lane. The drafting lane (Drafter interface, drafter.py:20-25; App.draft acting as ai:rule-drafter, app.py:53-62; governed by the door and policy) is driven by RuleDrafter, a deterministic word-overlap rule, not a model (drafter.py:1-8, 39-53; README.md:82). The rubric reads DEL-04 as inherently AI and rule-based behaviour as 0 in AI readings, so the stand-in is not credited as an AI lane. People implement each change by hand per installation through 'propose' (cli.py:60-63).
DEL-04.alt_note: If a governed rule-based drafting lane counted, it meets level 2: it drafts answers for one narrow task on request, through the same door, checks and policy, and a person approves (app.py:53-62; tests/test_release.py:36,43; tests/test_platform.py:92). Level 3 would still fail on breadth (answers only).

ai.evidence: No model ships (answerdesk/drafter.py:1-8; README.md:82,87). RuleDrafter is rule-based; the same anchors as the criterion, scored on model behaviour only.

DEL-05.evidence: Every definition change, including AI drafts and product proposals, passes deterministic pre-land checks in Door.check: kind validation, one change in flight, the regression suite for answers and routing rules, the raise rules for policy (door.py:98-119; checks.py:16-27; kinds.py:20-70), re-run at approval (door.py:61-68; tests/test_door.py:88,94). Gap: code changes have a unit-test suite (41 tests, all pass) but no gate in scope (no CI configuration in examples/born-evolvable). Checks changes are only validated (door.py:111-112).
DEL-05.alt_note: Every change class the evolution system makes (definitions) has an unskippable pre-land check with drafts included; only engineers' code changes lack an in-scope gate.

DEL-06.alt_note: For a local CLI, describe plus the restore integrity check cover most of a verification surface.

LRN-01.evidence: Every question is written synchronously as a signal with the version that served it and its exposures (desk.py:72-108; store.py:164-174) and is read at once by product features: evaluate, tick and unmet (door.py:185-217; scheduler.py:14-55; desk.py:115-122).
LRN-01.alt_note: Per-definition and per-version instrumentation is added automatically for every candidate change (exposures, desk.py:87-96), although nothing streams.

LRN-02.evidence: Typed signals: helpful/unhelpful feedback and a staff correction ('expected') per question (store.py:193-197; cli.py:50-57); answers link to the definition version that served them (answer_change, desk.py:98-103); measurement results link to the change (door.py:213-216). Routed questions record only the team, not the rule or its version (store.py:166-167), except through exposures to candidates. Triage: flagged failures become proposed checks a person approves (scheduler.py:38-45).
LRN-02.alt_note: For answers, signals are linked to definition and version, with a review workflow.

LRN-03.evidence: Failed outcomes are recorded and queryable with the area: unanswered questions with the team they went to, unhelpful feedback with the answer key and version (store.py:24-26, 164-174; cli.py:58-59). 'signals --unmet' groups unmet questions by exact text with counts (desk.py:115-122). Not 3: no issue objects, no affected-user counts, no friction patterns beyond a change's own measurement.
LRN-03.alt_note: Measurement detects a candidate change that worsens negative feedback against a control and raises it (door.py:185-217; scheduler.py:19-28), with frequency.

LRN-04.evidence: Usage, feedback and change history are joined inside the product for measurement and reversal (exposure_rows joins signals and exposures, store.py:203-208; evaluate, door.py:185-217; track_record from changes, door.py:257-260; wrong-pass events, scheduler.py:62-64). The operator queries them separately (signals, changes, audit: cli.py:58-59, 80-83); no joined queryable model.
LRN-04.alt_note: The joins used by measurement cover usage, feedback and change history.

LRN-05.evidence: For a reversed change the product attaches the failing questions (exposure rows), the measured rates and the check versions that passed it (scheduler.py:58-64; door.py:185-202). Not 3: no likely cause is produced for failures of stable definitions; the flagged-failure check proposal (scheduler.py:38-45) is a case, not a diagnosis.
LRN-05.alt_note: For change-induced failures it produces a reproducible case (a check from the first failed question) linked to the responsible change, for a person to confirm (scheduler.py:65-73; tests/test_release.py:68).

ai.evidence: No model ships (answerdesk/drafter.py:1-8; README.md:82,87). Rule-based grouping counts as 0.

LRN-06.evidence: Proposals for one area: checks from failures (scheduler.py:38-45, 65-73) and keep/revise/undo recommendations per change (door.py:197-212); answers for frequent unmet questions only at dial 5 (scheduler.py:47-54). Not ranked, no expected impact across the product.

ai.evidence: No model ships (answerdesk/drafter.py:1-8; README.md:82,87). Rule-based recommendations count as 0.

LRN-07.evidence: On each 'tick' the scheduler turns recorded experience into candidate changes without a per-item request: flagged failures and reversed changes become proposed checks (scheduler.py:38-45, 58-73); at dial 5 frequent unmet questions become drafted answers (scheduler.py:47-54; tests/test_loop.py:91). 'draft' generates a candidate on request (app.py:53-62). Nothing runs 'tick' on a schedule: it is a command (cli.py:78-79; README.md:42 'the product's scheduler, once').
LRN-07.alt_note: Run periodically, tick is a background review job that drafts changes unprompted.

ai.evidence: No model ships (answerdesk/drafter.py:1-8; README.md:82,87). Heuristic tuning counts as 0.

LRN-08.evidence: Product- and drafter-made changes pass the same pre-apply evaluation as any change: validation, then every check run against today's definitions and with the change applied; a regression blocks it (door.py:98-119; checks.py:16-27), plus the policy in code (policy.py:38-61). Re-run on approval (door.py:61-68). Tested: tests/test_door.py:88,94,104,110; the walkthrough rejects the same AI draft after the new check (walkthrough.py:90-95; tests/test_platform.py:109). The baseline set is small (two seed checks plus those grown from failures). Not 4: no held-out data; results do not feed the policy directly.

ai.evidence: No model ships (answerdesk/drafter.py:1-8; README.md:82,87). There are no model-made changes to evaluate; the checks that would apply are scored on the criterion.

LRN-09.evidence: Each release records baseline (from recent questions the change touches), target, window and tolerance (door.py:141-159; loop kinds door.py:167-173); evaluate compares candidate and control arms and records keep, revise, undo or waiting (door.py:185-217); the scheduler acts on it (scheduler.py:17-36). Tested: tests/test_release.py:36,43,68; tests/test_loop.py:73,81.
LRN-09.alt_note: Exposure instrumentation is created with each release and the policy's tolerance and the dial drive promote or reverse automatically; attribution limits are not recorded and loop changes are not reversed (DESIGN.md §11).

LRN-10.evidence: Checks and the policy are versioned kinds changed through the door (kinds.json:30-54). Results drive them: a reversal records a wrong_pass event against the check versions that passed the change and proposes a new check from the first failed question; flagged failures become proposed checks; a person approves at dial 3 (scheduler.py:38-45, 58-73; tests/test_release.py:68; tests/test_loop.py:10). The policy's raise rule reads the measured record and the product lowers a dial after reversals (policy.py:85-94; scheduler.py:75-87; tests/test_loop.py:46,54; tests/test_release.py:82). Not 4: check and policy changes are measured (door.py:203-212) but never reversed automatically (DESIGN.md §11, line 120), and adding checks needs a person at the default dial.

GOV-01.evidence: No user interface, component kit or accessibility scan in examples/born-evolvable (CLI JSON only, cli.py:104).

GOV-02.evidence: One audit table records proposals, policy decisions, checks, approvals, releases, switches, measurements, reversals and wrong passes with actor and time (store.py:149-161; door.py throughout), queryable by 'audit' (cli.py:82-83). Gaps: feedback, purge-signals, migrate, backup and restore are not audited (store.py:193-215; cli.py:86-91); no retention policy for events; rows are mutable.
GOV-02.alt_note: All definition changes and approvals are covered and an operator command queries them.

GOV-03.evidence: Signals only: emails and long numbers removed before storage, sessions hashed (desk.py:16-20, 74; tests/test_platform.py:56), retention via purge-signals (store.py:210-215; tests/test_platform.py:63). No field classification, no per-person export or erasure; free-text notes and event details are not redacted.

GOV-04.evidence: Validation is generic and mandatory for every kind (kinds.py:20-70 via door.py:100) and an actor-type policy applies to every change (policy.py:38-61), but there is no authentication: the CLI takes '--as person:NAME' on trust and the author may approve their own change (cli.py:33-36; README.md:89). No SAST, dependency or secret scanning in scope.
GOV-04.alt_note: A generic actor-type permission model and mandatory validation exist; only scanning and authentication are missing.

GOV-05.evidence: All four surfaces are versioned (store.py:82-139): 'changes --kind --key' shows every version with author, note, provenance, status and the version it replaced (cli.py:80-81), and 'undo' rolls back one step for every kind, audited (door.py:236-254), tested for each (tests/test_door.py:42,53,60,66,77). Scored 2 because no surface shows diffs (only whole versions), the drafter's sources/ are not versioned in the product, and 'migrate --to 0' destroys every version without audit (store.py:29; cli.py:88-89).
GOV-05.alt_note: History and rollback cover every customisation surface through a supported command; the versions are small JSON documents shown in full beside the one they replaced. Inventory levels are for this reading.

GOV-06.evidence: A change is a first-class row with body, note, provenance and status (store.py:16-20); people, the drafter and the product all propose (door.py:50-59); the check report previews outcomes with and without the change on a staged copy of the definitions (checks.py:16-27; door.py:113-118); a person approves, which re-runs policy and checks (door.py:61-68); release goes to a share first (door.py:128-134). Not 4: no preview on production-shaped data.

GOV-07.evidence: Policy object per kind of change with dial, limits, protected keys and daily cap (seed/policy.json:3-11; policy.py:38-61); approvals recorded as events (door.py:67).
